claims.text: The starting conventionally processed CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
WS2 nanoparticles can be incorporated into CoCrFeNi by powder metallurgy, such as spark plasma sintering, to form a composite.
Processing will produce a uniform distribution of WS2 nanoparticles within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The WS2 nanoparticles will be located both along grain boundaries and within grains.
Dispersed WS2 nanoparticles will enable formation of a lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
At lower temperatures, WS2 nanoparticles provide a low-shear-strength interface.
The low-shear-strength WS2 interface reduces friction at lower temperatures.
At elevated temperatures, WS2 partially oxidizes to form tungsten oxides.
The tungsten oxides formed at elevated temperature act as lubricious phases.
The proposed low-temperature WS2 lubrication and high-temperature oxide lubrication will maintain reduced friction and wear across the test regime.
WS2-reinforced CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
WS2-reinforced CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The reductions in coefficient of friction and wear rate will be sustained from room temperature through 800 °C.
Variability in nanoparticle dispersion and tribofilm-formation kinetics may alter the magnitude of the friction and wear reductions, particularly near 800 °C.
